- RTO/RPO attestation for the primary inference path (documented run and measured times for last three exercises)

- Warm-cache / KV cache warmup proof (logs or script output showing time-to-warm for a representative model)

- Point of contact for SOC 2 auditor if they need a verification call

We have prepared a short SIG workbook (attached) that maps controls to the requested artifacts. If you prefer, upload the files to the Drive link we shared during the call or send via secure SFTP.

On Tue, Jun 21, 2027 at 10:05 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben is looped in for the warm-cache proof — he has the test harness and can include raw outputs if you need them.

John —

I ran the warm-cache scenario we discussed during the May tabletop. A few technical details to set expectations so the artifact is useful for auditors:

- Our "time-to-ready" metric for warm-cache includes KV cache population plus a short token-step warmup (representative 512-token inference). Depending on model quantization and batch size that sits between 8–22s on a warm dedicated node in our last test.
- The runbook excerpt Rachel attached references the restore sequence; the warm-cache step is a node-local operation and the logs will show two phases (KV sync, then token warmup).
- We can supply a redacted log snippet and the measurement script we used. The logs include server timestamps (UTC) and a run id so auditors can correlate with the snapshot PDF.

I'll attach the two raw artifacts here: warm-cache-warmup-output.txt (redacted) and rto-measurement-script.sh (script used to capture the token warmup). If Sentinel wants raw traces from the serving runtime we will need an NDA amendment to share full traces — redacting is preferable to speed things up.

Attachments (stubs): warm-cache-warmup-output.txt, rto-measurement-script.sh

—Ben
